newsitem.title: USA: US W.Coast wholesale products edge up with futures.
newsitem.headline: US W.Coast wholesale products edge up with futures.

text.p: Wholesale prices for U.S. West Coast refined petroleum products edged up Thursday, tracking higher energy futures and increased buying in the local spot market.
After a quiet Wednesday session, higher values on the New
York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) inspired local traders to buy up barrels before prices increased further.

August unleaded gasoline futures rose 1.09 cents a gallon to 62.21 cents. Some futures traders speculated higher demand and an anticipated decline in supply from Tosco's huge New Jersey refinery prompted the rally.
Heating oil futures also climbed, with the front-month contract up 0.11 cents a gallon to 53.39 cents.
Traders offered August CARB gasoline in Los Angeles between 60/60.25 cents a gallon, with barrels sold at 60.25 cents, brokers said.
CARB diesel rose 0.50 cents to 56/57 cents a gallon, up a half cent from Wednesday.
State-mandated CARB gasoline was talked one cent higher than L.A., ranging between 61 cents and 62 cents.
